newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss bond market closing report.
newsitem.headline: Swiss bond market closing report.

text.p: Swiss bonds charged higher, with the Swiss government bond yield index dropping to levels last seen at the start of the year.
"We had an extremely strong price rise with very high volume. I can't remember last when we had such high volume," one Swiss bond trader said at the end of Wednesday's session.

A drop in long-term yields below 4.00 percent, a key level for Swiss pension funds, was a likely catalyst for the stampede into higher-yielding longer maturities. Traders said that at the same time, investors were selling the shorter end of the curve.

"It was notable that customers were selling the short end. People are willing to take higher risks. There were hardly any sellers," the trader said. He added that in the cash market, some federal bonds with longer maturities of eight to 12 years rose by nearly 90 ticks.
"Sentiment was an unbelievably positive. You could almost call it panic buying. People were simply seeking higher yields," he said.
Confederate bond futures volume totaled an estimated 3,600 contracts. The average yield of government bonds at midday was 3.77 percent, the lowest level seen since January.
Dec conf futures CONFZ6 up 64 at 114.94.
